critique: The render retains the correct black backdrop, dense warm fire palette, glow, and a visible downward progression from t1 to t4. However, it still reads as a compact, soft bead-like central plume instead of a broad field of individually falling sparks. At t4 the lower mass crowds into and clips at the bottom edge while the upper source remains narrow; the shower needs substantially more lateral distribution and less clustered particle scale.

suggestions.why: Widening the emitter creates a substantially broader spark source instead of the persistent tight center column.
Increasing directional spread pushes more particles outward as they fall, producing a scattered shower silhouette rather than a vertical plume.
Reducing particle size helps the dense field resolve as many distinct sparks rather than large soft, crowded beads.
